gen-fs-new-title-gf-biorhyme: Modern and tightly linked, New Title stands tall in its lowercase, like a fine chain pulled across the line. BioRhyme, a serif with brush-lifted curve endings, would sit nicely a few sizes down.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-domine: Lowercase letters locked together like links in a fine chain give New Title its tall, modern punch. Domine, a serif, handles the quieter job, with breathing space inside each curve and a lightly engraved contrast.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-lisu-bosa: Tight chain-link letters, tall and modern: that's New Title, a heading that stands up straight and means it. Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and open, its large lowercase carrying paragraphs without strain.
gen-fs-new-title-roboto-slab: New Title is tall, tightly linked and modern. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, gives the line a dense middle band, so size it up a notch for comfort.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-alpino: Small letters that stand nearly capital-sized, cut from wire: that is Nippo, technical through and through. Alpino is cozy and tight, better for a quick look than for paragraphs.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Proud little letters cut from wire: that's Nippo. Pilcrow Rounded packs tight spacing around big counters, warm enough for a quick paragraph but made for brevity, not a marathon.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-quicksand: Quicksand is all blown-glass bulbs and open endings. Next to Nippo, with its wire-cut, near-capital letters, it feels much gentler, a soft, friendly counterweight best kept to brief text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-ne: Wire-thin and proud, Nippo stands tall beside Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, whose washer-sized eyes and unlatched rounds feel contemporary and approachable. What stands out most is how clearly each letter speaks.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-roboto: Roboto reads clean, with generous mouths on its round letters. Nippo cuts every stem and curve from one gauge of tubing, while Roboto keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-stack-sans-headline: Small letters standing tall as capitals, cut from wire. Nippo is best at drawing the eye with near-capital lowercase, while Stack Sans Headline, a sans-serif with a monoline skeleton, keeps tiny sizes crisp.
